This system spans from short-term conversation history to long-term project and user-specific "memories." System Overview The persistence architecture consists of three primary subsystems: Memory System : Persistent, file-based storage for high-value insights (user preferences, project conventions) that should survive session restarts. Context Management : Real-time management of the active conversation context, including compaction and truncation to stay within token limits. Session Persistence : Logging and hydration of individual conversation threads, allowing users to resume or fork specific interactions. Context to Code Entity Mapping The following diagram illustrates how high-level persistence concepts map to specific implementation entities in the codebase. Persistence Architecture Sources: src/memdir/paths.ts 27 src/memdir/memdir.ts 34-38 src/query.ts 9-20 9.1 Memory System (MEMORY.md & memdir) Claude Code uses a structured, file-based memory system stored within the project's .claude/ directory. Memories are categorized into a four-type taxonomy: user , feedback , project , and reference src/memdir/memoryTypes.ts 14-19 Key Components: Memory Taxonomy : Constrains memory to information not derivable from the codebase itself (e.g., user role, specific testing preferences) src/memdir/memoryTypes.ts 4-7 The Index ( MEMORY.md ) : Acts as a high-level pointer system. The model reads this index to decide which specific topic files to fetch via FileReadTool src/memdir/memdir.ts 34-38 Extraction Subagent : A background process that analyzes the most recent messages to identify and save new memories using a specialized prompt src/services/extractMemories/prompts.ts 35-43 Team Memory : A shared memory directory for project-wide conventions, synced across different users of the same repository src/memdir/teamMemPaths.ts 84-86 For details, see Memory System (MEMORY.md & memdir) . Sources: src/memdir/memdir.ts 34-57 src/memdir/memoryTypes.ts 14-19 src/services/extractMemories/prompts.ts 1-10 src/memdir/teamMemPaths.ts 73-86 9.2 Context Compaction As a conversation grows, it eventually exceeds the model's context window or the user's defined token budget. Claude Code employs several "compaction" strategies to prune the history while retaining critical state. Compaction Pipeline Strategies: Microcompact : Inserts a boundary message to signal the model that older context is becoming less relevant src/utils/messages.ts 65 Autocompact : Automatically summarizes or removes older messages when token thresholds (e.g., ESCALATED_MAX_TOKENS ) are approached src/query.ts 9-12 Context Collapse : Collapses large tool outputs (like ls -R or long file reads) into summarized versions to save space src/query.ts 18-20 Reactive Compaction : A recovery mechanism that triggers when the API returns a 413 Request Too Large error, forcing an immediate context reduction src/query.ts 15-17 For details, see Context Compaction . Sources: src/query.ts 9-20 src/utils/messages.ts 59-69 src/utils/context.ts 89 9.3 Session Resume & Export Claude Code persists every session to a local JSONL log file. This allows for session recovery after a crash, terminal closure, or explicit use of the resume command. Features: Session Hydration : When a session is resumed, the system restores the message history, file edit history, and active todos src/query.ts 100 Forking : Users can "fork" a session, creating a new branch of the conversation from a specific point in time to explore alternative implementation paths. Exporting : The ExportDialog allows users to save the current transcript or memory state for external review or documentation. Token Budgeting : Sessions track token usage against a budget (e.g., +500k tokens), providing a getBudgetContinuationMessage when limits are reached src/utils/tokenBudget.ts 66-73 For details, see Session Resume & Export .
